author: Mycatdied
quote:
Grand Theft was, in fact, committed. Unfortunately, the victim was the franchise itself.

Everything that made GTA the legendary series it once was seems to have been thrown out the window in favor of an experience that feels less like an open-world crime sandbox and more like an aggressively supervised episode of The Real Housewives of Vice City.

GTA used to be about freedom. Glorious, ridiculous, unapologetic freedom. Steal cars, cause mayhem, ignore the rules, and do whatever the hell you wanted. It was an escape from reality, where the only limits were your imagination and how quickly the police could develop a personal vendetta against you.

Now? Apparently, it's about being put on rails, following someone else's schedule, doing chores, managing relationships, and getting lectured for failing to participate in your virtual domestic responsibilities.

If I wanted to be forced to do things with my significant other, run errands, complete household chores, and get griped at by my significant other, I'd simply turn off the game and return to my actual life. At least there, I might get some credit for taking out the trash.

I don't boot up GTA to experience a second job with better graphics. I don't need a virtual relationship counselor, a digital chore chart, or another reminder that I'm disappointing someone in yet another universe. Video games are supposed to be an escape from reality, not a second subscription to it. 

The whole appeal of GTA was that it let you live a ridiculous virtual life on your own terms. It was a sandbox, not a guided tour through somebody else's idea of how you should behave and spend your fictional free time.

Rockstar seems to have confused making a world feel alive with making the player feel obligated to participate in every mundane aspect of it.

Congratulations. You've taken a franchise built around freedom and turned it into a simulator where the biggest crime is apparently failing to do your damn chores.

Grand Theft Auto? More like Grand Theft Autonomy. And they stole every last bit of it.

author: Mycatdied
quote:
Best Diablo yet!  Thank you devs for not listening to the overly loud and snowflake minority that think internet forums and twitch streamers are the only voices for an entire player base.  It's always interesting to see that everyone is a professional game developer/business expert and knows every nuance of game design, balancing systems, etc.  If you don't do what the minority wants or if X streamer/youtuber stops playing then "dead game".  Get over yourself kids, the majority doesn't give a **** about patch notes, and something getting "nerfed" is not the end of the world, grow up.  Along those lines I find it funny when a "nerf" happens, people whine, but then realize there build is fine, if not still really good.  It's obvious that the game has content ready for the next several years and I for one look forward to playing each season till I get bored, move on to something else, and then come back for the next season.  Appreciate the work of all the Diablo team members, you knocked it out the park.

Combat - Easily best in the series and of any arpg on the market today.  Combat feels great, attacks almost have a weight to them, and it makes the repetition satisfying.  I also like that combat is somewhat slowed down (depending on the build).

World Design - Back to OG diablo with a dark setting.  I love the world map with the random events and dungeons.  Looking forward to what will be added in the future.

Campaign - Great story.  I agree there was a little filler around Acts 4 and 5, but overall satisfying story that kept me engaged, and now I want to see what's happening next.

Sound - Not much to say other than awesome.

Systems - Skills system and paragon tree is the perfect balance between robust but simplistic enough that any arpg enthusiast can understand how to craft their build.  No 3rd party apps needed here.

Endgame - For the first month of this live service game that planned early on to have seasons and introduce new systems with each season.  I think the end game was fine.  I imagine each season will continually add new "Uber" bosses and things to do.  I find it interesting that the core gameplay loop of Arpgs has not changed in years, but all the newbies cry....."It's boring, you do the same **** ****.  Its an arpg.

Cons (Although since this is a live service game, potential to be patched)

- While I applaud making gear only take up one grid square, I am finding my stash space and mules inventory quickly filling up.  I would love to see additional stash spaces.

- Would love to see a loot filter

- The CC at high NM Dungeon Tiers can get a little frustrating, depending on the elite you get, maybe diminishing returns on constant cc?

Don't worry Devs, the garbage will move on to something else soon and you'll be left with the real gamers.

author: Mycatdied
quote:
I think overall it's a fun game.  It is definitely hard to believe that it was made by Bungie, and that Activision put up $500 million to the IP, but it's fun none-the-less. Despite my below suggestions, this is still a game that I will play and probably continue to play due to my love of fps shooters with touches of rpg systems.  Bungie definitely has some work to do.

They need to go back to the drawing board in terms of voice actors (Peter Dinklage or whoever is horrible choice).  Less flavor of the month voice actors and more people that can actually portray the world you are trying to show us.

Artificial intelligence in this game is passable, but that's it.   I would definitely like to see this fixed in future iterations of the game.

Delivery of the story-line is horrid, but then again your choice in voice actors may be causing this issue.

Interface within vendors and the game menu is fine, but I would like to see it a little more polished, feels a little clunky.
